title: Sisi says Egypt is ready to defend Saudi Arabia 'if requested'; Yemen rebuffs Iran's mediation

title: Russia fires 332 drones in 'one of its largest' strikes on Ukraine's grid
summary: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 332 attack drones, including 31 jet-powered ones, four Kalibr cruise missiles, Kh-22/32 cruise missiles and Iskander-M or KN-23 ballistic missiles overnight into Oct 17, and that 289 drones were downed; strikes hit 22 locations. title: Republicans and Democrats condemn Trump's Russia sanctions waiver, but Congress is in recess

Democrats Elizabeth Warren and Don Beyer accused Trump of enabling Putin. Congress is in recess until after the Nov 3 midterms. Rep. Gregory Meeks's bill to revoke the OFAC licences behind the US-Russia diesel deal has 16 Democratic co-sponsors and Republican Rep. Don Bacon.

analysis.text: The backlash is real but toothless before Nov 3: a veto-proof majority is unlikely, so the waiver will stand through the winter strike season. The likelier result is that Europe takes over more of the sanctions and financing burden.

title: Starlink ground-station arson in Poland traced to a Turkish gang allegedly hired by Russian intelligence

Two Turkish citizens were arrested in Nürtingen, Germany, on Oct 12 on Polish warrants for sabotage on behalf of a foreign intelligence service; Poland's intelligence coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said there was 'no doubt' Russian services were behind it. causes.why: Both bear on Ukraine's satellite communications, which Russia is targeting by sabotage

title: France: 1,200 arrested as cost-of-living and school protests turn violent
summary: About 550,000 people marched across France on Oct 17 against hardship in schools and the cost of living, and at least 1,200 were arrested, the BBC reported. Attacks on EU diplomats raise the odds of European sanctions on settlers, while the outcome on Oct 27 will decide whether phase two of the Trump plan is revived or buried.

title: Lebanon's army delegation will demand an end to Israeli attacks at Oct 20 talks in Tampa
summary: Lebanon's presidency said on Oct 17 that a military delegation will present Beirut's demand for an end to Israeli attacks at a trilateral meeting with Israel and the US in Tampa, Florida on Oct 20. summary: Two brothers claiming allegiance to al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula attacked the satirical weekly; a linked gunman killed four at a kosher supermarket.

title: Houthi rebels force Yemen's President Hadi to resign
summary: After seizing Sanaa in September 2014 the Houthis put Hadi under house arrest; he escaped to Aden in February and withdrew his resignation.

title: Salman becomes king of Saudi Arabia and elevates his son Mohammed
summary: On King Abdullah's death Salman named his 29-year-old son defence minister, beginning MBS's rapid rise.

title: Kurdish YPG fighters backed by US airstrikes retake Kobani from the Islamic State
summary: The four-month siege was the group's first big defeat and began the US partnership with the Syrian Kurds.

title: Minsk II deal agreed as Russian-backed forces close on Debaltseve
summary: Merkel and Hollande brokered the ceasefire with Putin and Poroshenko. Fighting went on and Ukrainian forces withdrew from Debaltseve on Feb 18.

analysis.text: Minsk II froze the Donbas war on terms Kyiv never implemented; Putin declared it dead days before the 2022 invasion.

title: Islamic State in Libya beheads 21 Coptic Christians; Egypt bombs Derna
summary: The video showed the group's spread into Libya's chaos; it seized Sirte that year.
unplaced: Filmed on a Libyan coast, exact site unknown.

title: Opposition leader Boris Nemtsov is shot dead near the Kremlin
summary: The killing hours after he called for an anti-war march marked a new level of danger for Putin's critics.

title: Boko Haram pledges allegiance to the Islamic State
summary: Abubakar Shekau's pledge created the 'West Africa Province', which later split from his faction as ISWAP.

title: Gunmen kill 21 tourists at Tunis's Bardo museum
summary: In June a gunman killed 38 at a beach resort near Sousse, devastating Tunisia's tourism.

title: Saudi Arabia leads a coalition into Yemen's war against the Houthis
summary: Defence minister Mohammed bin Salman launched 'Decisive Storm' to restore Hadi; the war became a stalemate and a humanitarian catastrophe.

analysis.text: The war lies behind the Houthis' missile and drone arsenal and their later Red Sea campaign.

title: Muhammadu Buhari defeats Goodluck Jonathan, the first incumbent to lose in Nigeria
summary: The ex-general campaigned on beating Boko Haram and corruption.

title: Al-Shabaab gunmen kill 148 at Kenya's Garissa University
summary: The attackers singled out Christian students.

title: US warns of China's 'Great Wall of Sand' in the Spratlys
summary: China built artificial islands such as Fiery Cross Reef, later with runways and military facilities, despite Xi's pledge not to militarise them.

title: 7.8 earthquake in Nepal kills nearly 9,000
summary: The Gorkha quake devastated Kathmandu and the hills; India and China competed to lead the relief.

title: Protests erupt as Burundi's Nkurunziza seeks a third term
summary: A failed coup in May was followed by a crackdown and years of exile for hundreds of thousands.

title: Cameron wins a surprise majority, committing Britain to an EU referendum
summary: The Conservative manifesto had promised an in-out vote by 2017.

title: Islamic State captures Ramadi; days later it takes Palmyra in Syria
summary: Iraqi forces abandoned the Anbar capital and the group seized Syria's ancient city of Palmyra. It was the caliphate at its peak.

title: China launches 'Made in China 2025'
summary: Li Keqiang's plan aimed at self-sufficiency in chips, robotics, EVs and aerospace; Washington later cited it as a reason for the trade war.

title: Fifty nations sign up to China's Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
summary: Britain and other US allies joined despite Washington's objections; the bank financed parts of Xi's Belt and Road ambitions.

title: Greeks reject bailout terms 61–39, then Tsipras accepts a harsher deal
summary: With banks shut, Alexis Tsipras agreed a third bailout on Jul 13 to avoid leaving the euro.

title: Iran and world powers sign the nuclear deal in Vienna
summary: The JCPOA capped Iran's enrichment and stockpile in return for lifting nuclear sanctions.

analysis.text: Its 2018 abandonment by the US and Iran's later breaches set the path toward the 2025–26 strikes.

title: Suruç suicide bombing triggers the collapse of Turkey's peace process with the PKK
summary: The IS-linked attack killed 34 activists; days later the PKK killed two police officers and Turkey bombed PKK camps, ending a two-year ceasefire.

title: US and Cuba restore diplomatic relations and reopen embassies
summary: Obama's thaw ended 54 years of hostility; Trump reversed much of it from 2017.

title: Taliban founder Mullah Omar is revealed to have died in 2013
summary: Akhtar Mansour took over amid infighting.

title: Bombing at Bangkok's Erawan Shrine kills 20
summary: Police charged two Uyghur men, linking it to Thailand's deportation of Uyghurs to China.

title: China's stock crash triggers a global 'Black Monday'
summary: The bursting of the Shanghai bubble and a surprise yuan devaluation shook world markets.

title: Germany and Austria let stranded refugees in from Hungary
summary: Days after the photo of drowned toddler Alan Kurdi, thousands marched from Budapest; about 1.3 million people sought asylum in Europe that year.

analysis.text: The influx fuelled the rise of the AfD and anti-migration politics across Europe.

title: Presidential guard coup fails in Burkina Faso
summary: Mass protests and the army forced the plotters to give up within a week, and elections followed in November.

title: US regulators expose Volkswagen's diesel emissions cheating
summary: The EPA found software designed to fool lab tests; the scandal accelerated Europe's turn to electric vehicles.

title: Taliban briefly capture Kunduz, their first major city since 2001
summary: On Oct 3 a US gunship struck the MSF hospital there, killing 42.

causes.why: Mansour's new leadership sought a victory

title: Russia begins airstrikes in Syria to rescue Assad
summary: Flying from Khmeimim air base, Russian jets hit mainly non-IS rebels; it was Moscow's first war outside the former USSR since 1991.

analysis.text: The intervention kept Assad in power for nine more years and gave Wagner its first big theatre outside Ukraine.
